title: Fishing Mini-Game with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a fishing mini-game using Three.js with a physics debug overlay. Load the 'collision-world.glb' model using GLTFLoader as the environment/terrain around a fishing pond.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 8, 15) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (10, 20, 10) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- Load 'collision-world.glb' using GLTFLoader. Scale it to 0.5 and position it so it surrounds the scene as terrain. Center it at (0, -2, 0).
- Create a flat blue semi-transparent plane (20x20) at y=0 to represent the pond water surface. Use MeshStandardMaterial with opacity 0.6 and color 0x2288cc.
- Add subtle water animation by oscillating the water plane vertices with sine waves over time.
- Create a fishing rod as a group: a thin brown cylinder (radius 0.05, height 3) tilted at 45 degrees, with a white line (LineBasicMaterial) extending from the rod tip downward. Position the rod at (0, 1, 5).
- Create 5 fish as small colored ellipsoid meshes (scaled spheres, scale (0.5, 0.2, 0.3)) swimming beneath the water surface at random positions within the pond bounds (-8 to 8 on x, -8 to 8 on z, y between -2 and -0.5). Each fish should have a random color.

## Fish Physics & AI
- Fish swim in random patterns using simple steering: each fish has a velocity vector and changes direction every 2-4 seconds randomly. Speed should be between 0.5 and 1.5 units/sec.
- Fish are attracted to the hook (bait) when it is submerged within 3 units distance. They slowly approach the hook.
- When a fish is within 0.3 units of the hook and the hook is submerged, there is a bite event. The fish attaches to the hook.

## User Interactions
- **Spacebar**: Cast/reel the fishing line. First press casts (hook drops into water at a target point 5 units in front of the rod, animating downward to y=-1.5 over 1 second). Second press starts reeling (hook rises back up over 1.5 seconds). If a fish is attached, it comes up with the hook.
- **Arrow Left/Right**: Rotate the rod left/right around Y axis (rotate the rod group by 0.05 rad per frame while held), changing the cast target direction.
- **'D' key**: Toggle the physics debug overlay on/off.
- **Click a DOM button 'Reset'**: Reset the game state - all fish return to random positions, score resets, line reels in.

## Physics Debug Overlay
- When enabled, render wireframe bounding spheres around each fish (green if swimming freely, red if attracted to hook, yellow if caught).
- Show velocity vectors as arrows (ArrowHelper) from each fish center in their movement direction, length proportional to speed.
- Display a translucent sphere around the hook showing the 3-unit attraction radius.
- Show a small text sprite above each fish showing its distance to the hook (rounded to 1 decimal).

## HUD / DOM Elements
- A div with id='hud' in the top-left showing: Score (number of fish caught), current game state (idle/casting/waiting/reeling/fish_on), rod angle in degrees.
- A button with id='resetBtn' labeled 'Reset' in the top-right corner.
- A div with id='debugInfo' in the bottom-left showing (when debug is on): number of fish alive, fish velocities summary, hook position (x,y,z), and whether debug overlay is active.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- score: number (fish caught count)
- gameState: string ('idle'|'casting'|'waiting'|'reeling'|'fish_on')
- hookPosition: {x, y, z} - current hook world position
- hookSubmerged: boolean (hook y < 0)
- rodAngle: number (radians, starts at 0)
- fishCount: number (total fish in pond, decreases when caught and removed)
- fishStates: array of objects [{id, state: 'swimming'|'attracted'|'caught', distToHook, speed}]
- debugOverlay: boolean
- castCount: number (how many times player has cast)
- modelLoaded: boolean (true when collision-world.glb is loaded)
- waterAnimationTime: number (elapsed time for water animation)
- attractedFishCount: number (fish currently attracted to hook)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Fish velocities must remain bounded between 0 and 2 units/sec. Hook must not go below y=-3. Fish positions must stay within pond bounds (-9 to 9 on x/z). All position values must be NaN-free. Rod angle must stay within -PI/2 to PI/2. Attraction radius is exactly 3 units. Bite distance threshold is 0.3 units.
